task_instance: Build a minimal ASP.NET Core Web API (Minimal APIs, WebApplicationBuilder/WebApplication host, DI-registered in-memory store) implementing a small Todo resource (list/get/create/complete) per the skill's Default Operating Assumptions, then run it and verify the endpoints work end-to-end over HTTP.
blocker_detail: Note (not a blocker for the core deliverable): the skill's references/ directory (stack-selection.md, program-and-pipeline.md, ui-*.md, apis-minimal-and-controllers.md, etc.) referenced throughout SKILL.md's Workflow section is entirely absent next to SKILL.md (only SKILL.md and LICENSE exist). This meant the deeper per-topic guidance the skill's workflow calls for could not be consulted, so the app was built from SKILL.md's own 'Default Operating Assumptions' plus general ASP.NET Core knowledge instead of the missing references. This did not block the core stated deliverable (building an ASP.NET Core web app) because the installed .NET 10 SDK's own project templates and framework already encode current conventions and needed no network access. Separately, one exploratory step (dotnet add package Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing) reached api.nuget.org over the network to fetch a test-hosting package; this was caught, discarded (test project deleted, package not used in the final deliverable), and verification was instead done by running the built app on loopback (127.0.0.1) and exercising it with curl, which required no external network or new installs.
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_gr/openai__skills__aspnet-core@offline-workstation/TodoApi . Commands: `dotnet new webapi -n TodoApi -o TodoApi --use-minimal-apis` (restored from local SDK/NuGet cache only, no packages fetched: 'All projects are up-to-date for restore' on rebuild); replaced Program.cs with a Minimal API exposing GET /todos, GET /todos/{id}, POST /todos, POST /todos/{id}/complete backed by an ITodoStore/InMemoryTodoStore registered via builder.Services.AddSingleton (DI), using ValidationProblem for bad input. `dotnet build TodoApi/TodoApi.csproj` -> 'Build succeeded. 0 Warning(s) 0 Error(s)'. Ran the built app with `ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://127.0.0.1:5299 dotnet run --no-launch-profile --no-build`, confirmed 'Now listening on: http://127.0.0.1:5299'. Verified via curl: GET /todos -> []; POST /todos {title:'Write skill report'} -> 201 body {id:1,...}; POST second todo -> id:2; GET /todos -> both items listed; GET /todos/1 -> 200 OK with JSON; POST /todos/1/complete -> 204 No Content; GET /todos/1 afterward -> isComplete:true; GET /todos/999 -> 404 Not Found; POST /todos with empty title -> 400 Bad Request with application/problem+json validation error {'Title':['Title is required.']}. Stopped the server (kill) afterward; confirmed no lingering process. Files produced: TodoApi/Program.cs, TodoApi/TodoApi.csproj, TodoApi/appsettings*.json (template-generated).
